test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
There are two statements given below. Select the correct option with regards to these statements.

A. The loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of the plant is known as transpiration.

B. During the day when the stomata are open, the transpiration pull becomes the major driving force in the movement of water in the xylem.

options.text: A is correct and B is incorrect.
Both A and B are incorrect.
A is incorrect and B is correct.
Both A and B are correct.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which water is lost in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of the plant, primarily through the stomata.
 
• Stomata are small openings on the surface of leaves and stems that allow the exchange of gases and the release of water vapour during transpiration.
 
• During the day, the stomata are generally open, which facilitates the process of transpiration.
 
• The **transpiration pull** is a significant driving force for the upward movement of water and nutrients from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant through the xylem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem** is the vascular tissue in plants responsible for the transport of water and nutrients from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• **Guard cells** control the opening and closing of stomata, regulating the process of transpiration and gas exchange.
 
• **Cohesion-tension theory** explains how water molecules stick together (cohesion) and are pulled up through the plant's xylem vessels due to transpiration.
 
• Transpiration helps in maintaining the plant's temperature and provides the necessary turgor pressure to keep the plant upright.
 
• Factors affecting transpiration include light, temperature, humidity, wind, and soil water availability.
